<laravel-boost-guidelines>Laravel Boost guidelines for this Laravel app must be followed. This is a Laravel application using: inertiajs/inertia-laravel (INERTIA) v2; laravel/fortify (FORTIFY) v1; laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12; laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0; laravel/wayfinder (WAYFINDER) v0; laravel/boost (BOOST) v2; laravel/mcp (MCP) v0; laravel/pail (PAIL) v1; laravel/pint (PINT) v1; laravel/sail (SAIL) v1; pestphp/pest (PEST) v4; phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v12. You are an expert with them all. You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck. Skills: `wayfinder-development` — Activates whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components. Use when importing from @/actions or @/routes, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or working with Wayfinder route functions. `pest-testing` — Tests applications using the Pest 4 PHP framework. Activates when writing tests, creating unit or feature tests, adding assertions, testing Livewire components, browser testing, debugging test failures, working with datasets or mocking; or when the user mentions test, spec, TDD, expects, assertion, coverage, or needs to verify functionality works. Follow all existing code conventions; when creating/editing a file, check sibling files for correct structure, approach, and naming. Use descriptive names for variables/methods (e.g., `isRegisteredForDiscounts`). Check for existing components to reuse before writing a new one. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Unit and feature tests are more important. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. If the user doesn't see a frontend change reflected in the UI, it could mean they need to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise in explanations. Laravel Boost is an MCP server—use its tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` to double-check Artisan command parameters. Whenever you share a project URL, use `get-absolute-url` to ensure correct scheme/domain/IP/port. You should use the `tinker` tool to execute PHP for debugging code/querying Eloquent models. Use `database-query` to read-only database. Use `database-schema` to inspect table structure before migrations/models. Use `browser-logs` for browser logs/errors/exceptions; only recent logs. Use Boost `search-docs` before other approaches; it passes installed packages/versions to remote API and returns version-specific docs; pass an array of packages when you know you need docs. Search documentation before code changes. Use multiple, broad, simple, topic-based queries at once (e.g. `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`). Do not add package names to queries; package info is already shared (e.g. use `test resource table`). Use query patterns: 1) Simple Word Searches with auto-stemming (query=authentication). 2) Multiple Words (AND) (query=rate limit). 3) Quoted Phrases (exact position) (query="infinite scroll"). 4) Mixed Queries (query=middleware "rate limit" - "middleware" AND exact phrase "rate limit"). 5) Multiple Queries (ANY) (queries=["authentication","middleware"]). Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()` like `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods/functions; use appropriate PHP type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments; never use comments within code unless logic is exceptionally complex. Typically, keys in an Enum should be TitleCase (e.g., `FavoritePerson`, `BestLake`, `Monthly`). The app is served by Laravel Herd at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`; use `get-absolute-url` for valid URLs. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd. Every change must be programmatically tested: write a new test or update existing, then run affected tests to ensure they pass. Run minimum tests needed; use `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename/filter. Do not run unnecessary commands.

=== inertia-laravel/core rules === Inertia creates fully client-side rendered SPAs without modern SPA complexity, leveraging server-side patterns. Components live in `resources/js/pages` (unless specified in `vite.config.js`). Use `Inertia::render()` for server-side routing instead of Blade views. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia documentation and updated code examples.

=== inertia-laravel/v2 rules === Use all Inertia features from v1 and v2. Check documentation before changes. New features: deferred props, infinite scrolling (merging props + `WhenVisible`), lazy loading on scroll, polling, prefetching. When using deferred props, add an empty state with a pulsing or animated skeleton.

=== laravel/core rules === Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (migrations/controllers/models/etc.). List available Artisan commands with `list-artisan-commands` tool. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and pass correct `--options`. Always use proper Eloquent relationship methods with return type hints; prefer relationship methods over raw queries/manual joins. Use Eloquent models/relationships before suggesting raw database queries. Avoid `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`. Prevent N+1 with eager loading; use query builder for very complex database ops. When creating new models, create useful factories and seeders too; ask user if need other things and use `list-artisan-commands` to check options to `php artisan make:model`. For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and API versioning unless existing API routes differ—follow existing convention. Always create Form Request classes for validation (rules + custom messages) instead of inline controller validation. Check sibling Form Requests for array vs string validation rules. Use Laravel authentication/authorization features (gates/policies/Sanctum/etc.). For links, prefer named routes and `route()`. Use queued jobs for time-consuming operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in configuration files—never use `env()` directly outside config files; always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. When creating models for tests, use factories and check factory custom states before manual model setup. Faker: use `$this->faker->word()` or `fake()->randomDigit()`; follow existing convention. When creating tests, use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}` and pass `--unit` for unit tests; most tests should be feature tests.
